voiceover:
[curious] This Reddit tool made $38K in 30 days, with under $100K total ever.

And stay till the end, because the one move behind it is something you can copy today.

[conversational] It's called Bazzly. It finds Reddit posts where your SaaS fits, drafts a reply, and posts it for you. It costs $199 a month per project.

[confident] These numbers are verified on TrustMRR through Stripe. $35K a month in recurring revenue, 190 subscriptions, and 137% growth versus the previous period. But that's revenue, not profit.

The founder, Filip Panoski, failed at 5+ products over 7 years. Then he sat at $100 a month for 6 months. When growth got slow, he launched a new offer and went from $1K to $5K a month in two months.

[serious] The catch? The space is crowded, cheaper rivals exist, and Reddit moderators can remove promotional comments.

[whispers] Here's the move. He sells Reddit marketing, and he got customers by doing Reddit marketing himself, every day. No audience, no newsletter, no Product Hunt launch. Just a daily system in front of the right people.

[conversational] Would you build this or buy it? Send this to the friend who keeps "planning" their startup.

topic: Business breakdown: Bazzly — Get customers from Reddit on autopilot 🔥

pick.topic: Business breakdown: Bazzly — Get customers from Reddit on autopilot 🔥
pick.angle: A tool that gets customers from Reddit on autopilot hit $40K in 30 days, and the whole business is under $100K total revenue

research.what_it_does: A Reddit marketing platform for SaaS: it finds Reddit posts and Google-ranking Reddit threads where your product fits, drafts a reply, posts it from your own account or from an aged, warmed-up Bazzly account, adds upvotes, sends DMs to leads and tracks brand mentions (bazzly.ai/about).
research.who_pays: SaaS founders and small product teams who want customers from Reddit. The homepage plan is aimed at 'busy founders', and the Indie Hackers profile says it is for early-stage SaaS founders.
research.pricing: One plan, 'All in One', at $199/month per project with 170 credits that refresh monthly, plus a 7-day free trial with 5 credits. Credit costs: a post via a warmed-up account is 50, a comment via a warmed-up account is 10, an upvote is 0.2, and an AI draft is 0.1. Comments and DMs from your own account are free. Extra credits are $1 each. Each additional project costs $199/month and gets its own 170 credits (bazzly.ai homepage and /about). Older third-party pages list $19, $39 and $99 plans, so Bazzly appears to have raised its price over time.
growth: Founder-stated channels: 'Reddit (dogfooding Bazzly), X, and Indie Hackers' as distribution channels (Indie Hackers interview, 'After five failed products… hit $7.5k/mo in 12 months').

Per the same interview, once he hit $1k MRR he judged that growth would take about eight months to reach $3k MRR. He launched a new offer and grew from $1k to $5k MRR in two months using the same channels. The interview does not say what the offer was.
Per the same interview, he started building in public on X, Indie Hackers and Reddit only after he had real wins and proven strategies. He says that content kept driving organic traffic to Bazzly.
Founder's Indie Hackers post (June 2026): he crossed $2.5K MRR with 'No audience. No newsletter. No Product Hunt launch', and credits a daily system of marketing on Reddit.

X post, Sep 28 (2026, per the thread date): 'I sat at $100 MRR for 6 months. today: $15k MRR. nothing viral happened.' He says he did 4 things in order, but the 4 things were not visible in the source.
Founder DM playbook (X): reach out only to people who would actually want the offer, and lead with a personalized, value-first offer with no pitch. He says the same approach landed his partner Tibo.

Partnership and affiliates: Tibo (@tibo_maker) posted about Bazzly on X, and a third-party comparison blog says this sent a real wave of traffic (RunByte blog, a competitor, so treat as secondhand). On Oct 29, Tibo announced an affiliate program (bazzly.ai/affiliate). Filip cites $800 LTV and 50% trial-to-paid for the program on X.
Directory listings: Uneed launch on 2026-01-13, plus Micro SaaS Examples and bestreddit.tools listings.

Programmatic comparison and 'best of' pages on its own site: /compare/redship, /compare/crowdreply and /best-reddit-monitoring-tools, which ranks Bazzly #1 of 19 on its own checklist. This is an inference from the pages' existence; no source calls it an SEO strategy.
Social proof on the site: public customer reviews linked to original posts (17 per /is-bazzly-legit), including X posts saying it helps with GEO/AEO (showing up in AI answers).
founder_story: Filip Panoski founded Bazzly; his X bio says 'Quit my $7k/mo job to build SaaS' (X, Indie Hackers profile).

His site bio says he failed at 5+ products over 7 years that made $0 before Bazzly (kaijubeam.com bio, X post on Oct 29). In his Indie Hackers interview he says avoiding X and social media as an introvert for years cost him those seven years.
X post: '14 months ago I quit my job and lived on savings. Today I finally hit $1k MRR with Bazzly.'
Bazzly matched its first Reddit post for a customer on June 2, 2025 (/about).

Team: it is built by Filip and Tibo (Tibo Louis-Lucas, @tibo_maker, who has built and sold several bootstrapped products per the RunByte blog). It is operated by Meeteo Labs, LLC, a US company (/about).
lessons: Dogfood your channel. The product sells Reddit marketing, and the founder says he got customers by doing Reddit marketing himself, plus X and Indie Hackers.
Don't build an audience first. Build a daily system that puts you in front of the right people. He reached $2.5K MRR with no audience, newsletter or Product Hunt launch.
Change the offer when growth is slow. He projected 8 months to get from $1k to $3k MRR, then launched a new offer and hit $5k in two months through the same channels.
Share only proven results. He started building in public after he had real wins to show, so the content came from real experience.
Value-first DMs work for customers and partners. He says the same personalized, no-pitch DM got both customers and his co-founder Tibo.
Plan for years, not months. He sat at $100 MRR for 6 months before it took off, and failed at 5+ products before that.
criticism: The category is crowded. Bazzly's own comparison pages name RedShip, CrowdReply, ReplyAgent, RedReach, Replymer, RedditGrow, KWatch.io, MediaFast and Subreddit Signals. Cheaper rivals exist, e.g. RunByte at $19/mo (competitor's claim).

Platform risk: moderators can remove promotional comments on Reddit. Bazzly says it refunds warmed-account comments removed within 48 hours (/is-bazzly-legit). Competitors say its auto-posting through aged accounts puts accounts at risk, which is a biased source, and a reviewer site notes automated replies and DMs can read as spammy.
Revenue is not profit. No cost or profit data was found.

Some of the founder's self-reported numbers have been challenged. A commenter on his Indie Hackers post (June 2026) said TrustMRR then showed $1,131 MRR with 39 subscriptions against his claimed $2.5K. The founder replied that he had linked TrustMRR in the post. His bio MRR also varies by snapshot ($15k, $17k, $23k), so use the Stripe-verified numbers.
Reddit-only: Bazzly's own page concedes it is Reddit only and offers a free trial, not a free plan.
His Indie Hackers interview says part of his earlier revenue was one-time payments inside the platform: $5k MRR plus $2.5k in monthly expansion revenue. That is not recurring.
facts: 1,235 brands had been set up in Bazzly by October 12, 2026 (/is-bazzly-legit).
It has an MCP server (Streamable HTTP), a REST API and a Chrome extension (compare pages and /is-bazzly-legit).
Bazzly's compare page says CrowdReply charges $7 to $10 per comment, against 17 warmed-account comments included in Bazzly's $199.
An Indie Hackers headline says he reached $7.5k/mo in 12 months. That figure was MRR plus expansion revenue, as noted above.
Founder X post: 'almost every day people are switching from our competitors to Bazzly' (self-reported).
do_not_claim: Team size beyond Filip and Tibo, or any equity or ownership split
What the '4 things' behind $100 to $15k MRR were, or what the new $1k to $5k offer was
Any virality: the founder says 'nothing viral happened'
That Bazzly is bootstrapped or has no funding (no source states it)
That Reddit comments never get banned or removed. 'Zero ban risk' is marketing copy, and the site itself offers removal refunds.
That the affiliate program or Tibo's post drove any specific revenue number
The $19, $39 or $99 prices as current. They are from older third-party pages.

real_pages.show: Get Customers From Reddit on Autopilot

research.notes: Use the TrustMRR figures for revenue (MRR $35,130, 190 subscriptions). Founder bios and posts show older, stale MRR numbers ($15k, $17k, $23k), so don't quote them as current. The official price is $199/month; many third-party sites still show $99 or $19. The founder is on X as @FilipPanoski, and the TrustMRR record's founder_x field was empty. The competitor-run sites (RunByte, Reppit) are biased sources. Treat the claim that Tibo's X post sent a wave of traffic as secondhand. Bazzly's 'best of' rankings are self-ranked. Safe hook: a solo founder who failed at 5+ products over 7 years and sat at $100 MRR for 6 months, now at $35k MRR by dogfooding Reddit marketing.
